annotation.title_clean: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.title_en: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States Congress (Cornell Legal Information Institute reproduction)
annotation.venue: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute (US Code)
annotation.summary_en: US statute (49 U.S.C. § 44810) directing the FAA to plan certification and testing of counter-drone detection and mitigation systems at airports, exempting authorized activities from certain criminal and surveillance laws, with annual congressional briefings and a sunset of September 30, 2028.
key_provisions_or_claims: FAA must develop a plan to certify or authorize drone detection and mitigation systems.
FAA must test such systems at five airports, including one in the top 10 by boardings.
Airport sponsors may use airport improvement grants to purchase approved systems.
Authorized activities are exempt from certain criminal and surveillance statutes.
Authority cannot be delegated to other agencies; section sunsets September 30, 2028.
